office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Open Vancouver seat, the first in 15 years, after Rep. Sharon Wylie ran for county auditor. Democrat Kim Harless, a two-term Vancouver City Council member endorsed by The Columbian, faces Republican Sarah Mittelman, a psychiatric nurse practitioner and former chair of the Clark County Democratic Women; they split on the tax on income over $1 million, I-638, spending and state housing-siting rules.

candidates.summary: Two-term Vancouver City Council member and nonprofit policy director who co-chaired the 2021 county charter review, running on progressive revenue, tenant protections, climate action and universal healthcare.
highlights: Would defend the tax on income over $1 million and the capital gains tax and expand taxes on concentrated wealth [S2]
Wants rent stabilization with a lower cap than the 2025 law, just-cause eviction and social housing [S2]
Urges a no vote on I-1 and I-638; defends comprehensive sex education and gender-affirming care access [S2]
Backs the Washington Health Trust for a unified system covering all residents and the SAFE Act on immigration enforcement [S2]
Endorsed by The Columbian's editorial board [S6]

taxes.basis: Platform defends the tax on income over $1 million and seeks more wealth taxes; says she passed Vancouver's first B&O tax.

spending.basis: Would direct new revenue to housing, education, healthcare and the public workforce, restore child-care funding and move toward free community college.

housing.basis: Platform centers rent stabilization, tenant protections and social housing; city record also includes supply measures (MFTE expansion, removing parking minimums).

safety.basis: Favors co-responders, civilian crisis response and civilian traffic enforcement, while her city record also includes body cameras and police and fire funding measures.

climate.basis: Would defend the Climate Commitment Act and adopt a climate superfund; championed Vancouver's carbon-neutrality framework and a bulk fossil-fuel storage moratorium.

experience.basis: Two terms on the Vancouver City Council and charter review co-chair; first run for the Legislature.

reform.basis: Supports ranked choice and proportional ranked choice voting and led the charter review effort to put RCV on the ballot.

immigration.basis: Would pass the SAFE Act limiting federal immigration enforcement in sensitive places, fund deportation legal defense and lists immigrant rights as a priority.

healthcare.basis: Would champion the Washington Health Trust for a unified system covering all residents; pamphlet lists universal healthcare.

social.basis: Would protect abortion access, gender-affirming care and the shield law, opposes I-638; endorsed by Pro-Choice Washington and Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates.

parental-rights.basis: Urges a no vote on I-1, saying it would force schools to out LGBTQIA+ students, and would defend comprehensive sex education; her council voted to oppose I-1.

tech.basis: Wants ratepayers protected from data-center infrastructure costs with energy and water transparency, and further limits on surveillance tools such as Flock cameras.

candidates.summary: Psychiatric mental health nurse practitioner with 20 years in emergency, behavioral health and homeless-outreach care, a first-time candidate and former Clark County Democratic Women chair now running as a Republican, on accountability for spending and behavioral-health outcomes.
highlights: "No blank checks without measurable outcomes"; would review programs before expanding costs [S2]
Supports I-638: "Biological males should not compete in girls sports" [S5]
Opposed HB 2266's state siting rules for supportive housing as lacking local input [S6]
Calls for more detox and stabilization capacity, involuntary treatment when clinically necessary and accountability for repeat offenders [S8][S2]
Campaign video sets out concerns about the new income tax [S3]

taxes.basis: Campaign video presents concerns about the tax on income over $1 million; pledges to protect families and small businesses from unnecessary financial burdens.

spending.basis: Repeatedly calls for measurable outcomes before new spending, including in Clark County homelessness programs.

safety.basis: Pairs expanded treatment capacity with involuntary treatment when clinically necessary and accountability for repeat offenders and traffickers.

local-control.basis: Opposed HB 2266's limits on local governments' siting authority for supportive housing; says state policy should reflect local voices.

social.basis: Supports I-638 on sex-based girls' sports while calling for opportunities for transgender students; no position found on abortion or gender-affirming care.

experience.basis: No elected experience; the Columbian describes her as a political newcomer.
